chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Key men in the DeLisa band
summary: Sonny Cohn, Earl Washington, Walter Cole, Porter Kilbert, Harlan Floyd, Johnnie Board, Gene Ammons, Cy Touff, Dennis Farnon and Marty Martinez.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were some of your key men?

Well, some of the key men, like Sonny Cohn, he's with Basie, I brought him in at that particular time, and then I had Earl Washington, well, he was a former brother-in-law of mine, and --on piano, and I had the boy now who's with the Trendiers, Walter Cole, he was on bass. And on saxes, we had Porter Kilbert. Did you ever know Porter?
I didn't know him, but I've heard him play.
He was one the great -- he used to work with Benny Carter, and he worked with Quincy Jones' band.
He worked a short while with Ellington, too.

Right, right, right. And so we had he and Harlan Floyd, Booby, he went with Basie, he worked with me, Johnnie Board. And it was just so many musicians that went through the band, and then Gene, Gene would come in and play with us occasionally, Gene Ammons. Yeah, he worked with us at times.

And then, -- well, all the musicians that we had, they'd come and they would go, for different reasons -- Army, different things. But we had quite a few musicians that as the years go by you kind of forget about them until you see them again. Right, and we had good trombones, Cy Touff, Dennis Farnan, you remember we was talking about Dennis Farnan, and Cy Touff, and Marty Martinez. I don't know whether you knew him, he was a Spanish guy, plays trombone very good.
So we always kept an -- but it didn't make any difference, because the club was an integrated club. So far as clientele was concerned.
